message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide you can copy into your favourite tool (curl, Postman, Python `requests`, JavaScript `fetch`, etc.) to pull **only** the file identifiers (plus whatever “context” metadata the service returns) for everything that has been pulled down from *downloads.com* under your API key (`dload_key`).  

> ⚠️  
> Replace `<BASE_URL>` with the actual root address given in the Downloads.com developer docs – e.g., `https://api.downloads.com`.  
> If the API uses OAuth2 instead of raw keys, swap out the `Authorization` line below for the appropriate bearer token flow.

---

### 1️⃣ One‑liner curl command

```bash
curl -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "X-DL-Key: dload_key" \          # <-- custom auth header used by many APIs
     "https://<BASE_URL>/v1/downloaded-files?sourceDomain=downloads.com"
```

If the service expects the key in the querystring instead:

```bash
curl -G --data-urlencode apikey="dload_key" \
      "https://<BASE_URL>/v1/downloaded-files?sourceDomain=downloads.com"
```

Both will return something like:

```json
{
  "total": 42,
  "page": 1,
  "per_page": 20,
  "items": [
    { "id":"f12345",   "filename":"report.pdf",   "size_bytes":102400 },
    { "id":"f67890",   "filename":"image.png",    "size_bytes":204800 }
  ]
}
```

Only the `"id"` field is required; all other properties (“context”) are optional but useful for debugging.

---

### 2️⃣ Example in Python (`requests`) – just IDs + minimal context

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "dload_key"
BASE_URL  = "https://<BASE_URL>"
ENDPOINT  = "/v1/downloaded-files"

params = {
    "sourceDomain": "downloads.com",
    "fields": "id,name,size_bytes",   # request only needed columns
}

headers = {
    "Accept":        "application/json",
    "Content-Type":  "application/json",
    "X-DL-Key":      API_KEY            # adjust header name per spec
}

resp = requests.get(BASE_URL+ENDPOINT, params=params, headers=headers)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()

file_ids = [item["id"] for item in data.get("items", [])]
print(file_ids)

# Optional: print extra context info
for item in data.get("items", []):
    print(f"id={item['id']}, filename={item.get('name')}")
```

#### Pagination helper

Most services cap results at ~100–200 items per page. Add `page=` & `limit=` parameters until no more pages remain:

```python
def fetch_all_file_ids():
    ids = []
    page = 1
    while True:
        r = requests.get(
            BASE_URL+ENDPOINT,
            params={"sourceDomain":"downloads.com","page":page,"limit":50},
            headers=headers
        )
        r.raise_for_status()
        batch = r.json().get("items", [])
        if not batch:
            break
        ids.extend([i["id"] for i in batch])
        page += 1
    return ids
```

---

### 3️⃣ Using JavaScript/Node.js (`node-fetch`)

```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');

async function listFileIds() {
  const res = await fetch(`https://<BASE_URL>/v1/downloaded-files?sourceDomain=downloads.com`,
                          { headers: { 'X-DL-Key': 'dload_key',
                                       Accept: 'application/json'}});
  const json = await res.json();
  console.log(json.items.map(i=>i.id));
}
listFileIds();
```

---

### 4️⃣ Quick checklist before running

| ✅ Item | What to verify |
|--------|----------------|
| Base URL | Confirm it matches the production environment (`api.downloads.com`) |
| Endpoint path | `/v1/downloaded-files` (or similar) |
| Auth method | Header vs query param; check docs |
| Query params | `sourceDomain=downloads.com`; add `fields=id` if supported |
| Rate limits | Respect X‑RateLimit-* headers |

Once you hit the endpoint successfully, you'll receive a JSON payload where each object contains at least an `"id"` property plus any additional context the API chooses to expose (e.g., `"created_at"`, `"status"`, `"owner_id"`).

Feel free to tweak the `fields=` parameter so you only download what you actually care about—this keeps bandwidth low and speeds up subsequent processing steps.
